dispatches.topic: Hidden Hazards in DIY Flipped Homes
dispatches.subject: Pitch: Why Flipped Home Makeovers Conceal Structural & Electrical Hazards (Christopher Boykin, CMI®)
dispatches.expertBio: Christopher Boykin, Certified Master Inspector (CMI®) and founder of Foresight Home Inspections, LLC (Atlanta, GA). Led by fewer than 1% of inspectors in North America.
dispatches.soundbite: Cosmetic flippers excel at quartz countertops and luxury vinyl plank flooring, but our dual-inspector teams routinely find unpermitted electrical double-taps inside breaker panels, non-vented plumbing drains hidden behind shiplap, and fresh coats of drylock paint sealing active structural foundation shears.
dispatches.keyStat: Over 65% of fast-flipped homes exhibit at least one major unpermitted electrical or plumbing compromise.

dispatches.topic: The ROI of Sewer Scope Inspections in Older Neighborhoods
dispatches.subject: Pitch: Why a $450 Sewer Scope Saves Atlanta Home Buyers $15,000+ (Christopher Boykin, CMI®)
dispatches.expertBio: Christopher Boykin, Certified Master Inspector (CMI®) and founder of Foresight Home Inspections, LLC (Atlanta, GA). Led by fewer than 1% of inspectors in North America.
dispatches.soundbite: Standard visual home inspections stop where plumbing lines enter the concrete slab or ground. In established 1950s–1980s neighborhoods, tree root intrusion and heavy clay soil shifting crush aging clay and cast iron laterals. A high-resolution sewer camera is the single highest-ROI diagnostic a buyer can order.
dispatches.keyStat: Underground sewer line excavation and replacement in Metro Atlanta routinely costs between $5,000 and $15,000.

dispatches.topic: Georgia Red Clay Soil & Foundation Settlement Dynamics
dispatches.subject: Story Idea: How Georgia Red Clay Drought-to-Storm Cycles Fracture Suburb Foundations
dispatches.expertBio: Christopher Boykin, Certified Master Inspector (CMI®) and founder of Foresight Home Inspections, LLC (Atlanta, GA). Led by fewer than 1% of inspectors in North America.
dispatches.soundbite: Georgia's expansive kaolinite and illite red clays act like hydraulic sponges. During prolonged summer heat, the soil shrinks away from foundation stem walls. When torrential autumn storms hit, the rapid re-expansion exerts uneven lateral shear force, creating the telltale stair-step brick cracks and binding doors we see across Gwinnett, Fulton, and DeKalb counties.
dispatches.keyStat: A minimum 6-foot downspout extension away from the foundation reduces soil hydrostatic pressure by over 70%.

dispatches.topic: Radon Gas Penetration in North Georgia's Granite Belt
dispatches.subject: Expert Commentary: Why 1 in 3 North Metro Atlanta Homes Exceed EPA Radon Safety Limits
dispatches.expertBio: Christopher Boykin, Certified Master Inspector (CMI®) and founder of Foresight Home Inspections, LLC (Atlanta, GA). Led by fewer than 1% of inspectors in North America.
dispatches.soundbite: Because the North Metro area sits directly over the Stone Mountain and Piedmont granite geological formations, decaying uranium in the bedrock continually vents odorless radon gas upward into basements, crawlspaces, and concrete slabs. Continuous 48-hour electronic testing is critical before closing.
dispatches.keyStat: The EPA action threshold is 4.0 pCi/L, yet homes across Fulton, Cobb, and Gwinnett regularly test at 6.0 to 14.0 pCi/L.
